title: Model scenes: W/WASD desyncs the orbit camera (lighting shifts until you orbit) and near-side wireframe edges z-fight away
description:
Two rendering bugs in orbit-camera model scenes, both seen in the mesh-boolean scene (`MeshBooleanScene`, where W toggles the wireframe).

**1. W changes the lighting; orbiting restores it.** W is bound twice. `OrbitCameraKeyGuy.handleSceneKeys` fires the scene's `ControlHint` (toggle wireframe), and `KeyGuy.paintUpdate` also runs `Camera2DInputController.apply` every frame, where `KeyActions.MoveUp` is W. That calls `Camera3D.move(FORWARD)`, which moves `position` along the free-fly `front` vector (from the camera's stale yaw/pitch; the orbit never sets it) and then `updateCameraVectors()` overwrites `target = position + front` and `up`. The view matrix is not rebuilt (only `OrbitMouseTrap.applyOrbit` does that), so the geometry does not move. But `HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.render` derives `lightDir` from `camera.target - camera.position`, which is now the stale `front`, so the camera-following light swings. `nearPlaneFor`/`farPlaneFor` also read `position.distance(target)`, which is now 1. The next drag or scroll calls `applyOrbit()`, which resets position and target, so the lighting comes back. A, S and D (MoveLeft/MoveDown/MoveRight) do the same, and D is also mesh-boolean's "difference" key. Every `ModelScene` using `OrbitCameraKeyGuy` is affected, not only mesh-boolean.

Likely fix: orbit scenes should not run the free-fly WASD camera movement. Either `OrbitCameraKeyGuy` overrides `paintUpdate` to skip `Camera2DInputController.apply`'s move keys, or a key consumed by a ControlHint is kept out of `pressedKeys` movement. Separately, `HalfEdgeMeshRuntime` could take the light direction from the view matrix instead of position/target, so it can never disagree with what is drawn.

**2. You see edges on the far side of the model but not the near side.** `HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.renderEdges` draws every edge twice. The faint pass has depth test off, so far-side edges show through the model by design. The bold pass has depth test on but never sets `depthBias`, so it draws at exactly the faces' depth (PATCH-17 only biases `renderFeatureEdgeOverlay`, with 0.0003). Under GL_LESS the near-side bold edges z-fight with the faces they lie on and mostly disappear, which leaves the faint far-side edges as the only visible lines. Likely fix: set `meshUnlitShader.setFloat(DEPTHBIAS, NUM_0_0003)` for the bold pass and reset it to 0 afterwards, as the feature-edge overlay does. Also reconsider whether the faint depth-off pass should stay on by default. Confirm in a screenshot that this is what the user sees. If instead whole front *faces* are missing, check the boolean output's winding/normals (`display.computeNormals()` in `MeshBooleanScene.applyProvenanceTags`) and the depth state.

Side note: in `mesh.fs` the rim term uses world-space `n.z`, so it does not follow the camera. Not this bug, but a candidate to fix alongside it.
definition-of-done:
1. In mesh-boolean, pressing or holding W (and A/S/D) changes nothing except the bound control: the lighting and the near/far planes stay the same before and after, and dragging afterwards does not cause a lighting jump.
2. The orbit target and position in Camera3D are only ever written by OrbitMouseTrap in ModelScene subclasses that use OrbitCameraKeyGuy.
3. With wireframe on, the near-side edges are drawn clearly on top of the faces and the far-side edges read as fainter than them.
4. A `.vscode/launch.json` entry for mesh-boolean, and before/after screenshots under `tmp/` (wireframe on, after pressing W, and after orbiting).
testing-plan:
1. Launch mesh-boolean, take a screenshot, press W twice (wireframe off and on again), and take another screenshot. The shading must be identical apart from the edges.
2. Hold W for a second, then drag-orbit slightly and back. The shading must not jump.
3. Zoom in on one cube face with wireframe on and check that its edges are solid red, not broken up by z-fighting.
unknowns: Is the 'can't see the front side' report about the wireframe edges (z-fighting, likely) or about whole faces? Confirm with a screenshot before fixing.
changes-made: Bug 1 (W/A/S/D shifted the lighting until you orbited): OrbitCameraKeyGuy now overrides paintUpdate to apply only the =/- zoom keys (new Camera2DInputController.applyZoom), so orbit scenes never run free-fly Camera3D.move and OrbitMouseTrap is the only thing that sets position/target. HalfEdgeMeshRuntime now takes lightDir from the view matrix (view.positiveZ negated), so the light always matches what is drawn. Verified: a frame after pressing W twice is pixel-identical to the start frame (it was 39% different before); tmp/view-9-before-*.png vs tmp/view-9-after-*.png. Bug 2 (near-side wireframe edges hidden): confirmed as z-fighting, since before the fix the red edges were dashed and broken while every face rendered. renderEdges' bold pass now uses depthBias 0.0003, like the feature-edge overlay, and resets it to 0 afterwards. Near edges are now solid red (tmp/view-9-after-zoom.png); far edges show only as the faint depth-off pass. mesh.fs: the rim term now uses the view-space normal z, so it follows the camera. Launch entry 'VIEW-9: mesh-boolean'.
